title: The Cracks in the Feigned Death Begin to Show
next_chapter_hook: The familiar handwriting flickered in the candlelight, as if coming from a long-forgotten old friend...

text.content: Night wind like a blade, in the ruined temple at the west corner of the imperial capital, Chen Ji sat alone before the broken deity statue, fingertips gently stroking the Tianji Record Fragment. Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul floated within the pages, speaking mournfully: "Three forces are closing in on you simultaneously—this is no good omen." Chen Ji did not answer, merely casting his gaze toward the pitch-black street outside the window—Xuanwu Sect's secret agents were just then three hundred steps away in a teahouse.

He closed his eyes, and the patterns on the Tianji Record Fragment glowed faintly. Scenes from the next three hours surged like a tide—within an elegant room on the second floor of the teahouse, a middle-aged man in a blue robe was unrolling a portrait, and the face depicted was precisely Chen Ji's. Below the portrait was a line of small text: "Alive or dead, we must see the person. Xuanwu Sect offers a reward of three thousand spirit stones."

dialogue.content: Three thousand spirit stones... they do put a high price on my face.

text.content: Chen Ji opened his eyes, a derisive curve forming at the corner of his mouth. The Heavenly Fate had been consumed by another 5 points, leaving him with less than a hundred remaining. Each glimpse into the future was like burning away his own life force. Yet if he didn't know the dangers in advance, how could he survive this game of chess? Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out again with a note of warning: "Lad, the Crown Prince's faction has sent someone too, and they're more troublesome than the Xuanwu Sect."

Almost at the same moment, soft footsteps sounded outside the ruined temple. Chen Ji's gaze sharpened abruptly, yet he did not move. His concealment formation was sufficient to deceive cultivators below the Golden Core stage, but if the visitor was one of the Crown Prince's shadow guards... The footsteps halted at the door, followed by a neatly folded piece of paper being slipped through the crack.

dialogue.content: (In a low voice) The messenger has left?

text.content: Mo Xiansheng said: "Gone. Their cultivation isn't high, but their lightness skill is exceptional—typical of shadow guards." Chen Ji walked slowly to the door and picked up the paper. The paper was coarse, evidently deliberately chosen for its unremarkable appearance. But when he unfolded the letter and saw its contents, his entire body was struck like by thunder.

The letter contained only a few sparse words, yet each character cut like a blade: "The Grand Tutor is not dead, buried in the chaotic graves at the city's east. In three days, Xuanwu Sect and Crown Prince's residence will jointly excavate the tomb for verification. If Brother Chen wishes to avoid exposure, he must make a decision within three days." At the letter's end, there was no signature—only a symbol drawn: a soaring cyan phoenix, overlapping with some vague image buried in Chen Ji's memory.

dialogue.content: (Fingers trembling slightly) This symbol... impossible, how could she...

text.content: A thought flashed through Chen Ji's mind like lightning. That symbol—he had seen it in his long-missing sister Chen Nian's diary. He had believed that diary had turned to ash in the flames of war, yet never imagined it would resurface in this manner. Coincidence, or was someone deliberately guiding this?

choice.prompt: The encirclement of the three forces was tightening, and Chen Ji had to make a choice: continue hiding and wait for the right moment, take the initiative to disrupt the enemy's arrangements, or set a trap to turn the tables?

choices.description: Temporarily withdraw from the imperial capital, observe the movements of all parties from the shadows, and wait for a better opportunity. Lower risk, but may lose the initiative in the situation.
choices.visible_cost: May lose control over the Crown Prince's residence investigation
choices.risk_hint: The tomb excavation verification in three days cannot be prevented

text.content: Chen Ji coldly smiled, tucking the letter into his sleeve. Conceal and lie in wait? In this game of chess, passive waiting was never his style. But indeed, he needed to first leave this dangerous place. He swiftly gathered his belongings and quietly departed through a secret passage under Mo Xiansheng's guidance.

dialogue.content: (Mo Xiansheng) What do you plan to do? Just watch them dig open that empty tomb?

choices.description: Strike first, directly negotiate with or eliminate the Xuanwu Sect's secret agents. Higher risk, but can regain the initiative in the situation.
choices.visible_cost: May expose more strength and invite greater troubles
choices.visible_reward: Resolve the Xuanwu Sect threat in one stroke, deterring other forces
choices.risk_hint: There may be a greater force backing the Xuanwu Sect

text.content: A fierce glint flashed in Chen Ji's eyes. Concealment was never his style. Since they wanted to seek death, he would grant them their wish. He rose, straightened his clothes, and the familiar expression of atrash appeared on his face—timid, cowardly, utterly harmless. Yes, this was his best mask for navigating the world.

dialogue.content: Mo Xiansheng, don't you feel that there are always some people in this world who like to treat others as fools?

choices.description: Using the false death identity and the contradictions among various parties, set a trap to let them exhaust each other. Medium risk, potentially maximum gain.
choices.visible_cost: Requires meticulous planning, any misstep could lead to total failure.
choices.visible_reward: Turn Xuanwu Sect against the Crown Prince's Residence, killing two birds with one stone.
choices.risk_hint: If exposed, would simultaneously offend two major powers.

text.content: Chen Ji sat back down, fingertips tapping the table as his mind raced. The Xuanwu Sect wanted his life, the Crown Prince's Residence wanted to uncover the truth, and that anonymous letter... if he could use it wisely, perhaps he could make them turn on each other. A slight smile curved his lips as a bold plan gradually took shape.

dialogue.content: (Mo Xiansheng) You want the people from Xuanwu Sect and the Crown Prince's Residence to meet before that empty tomb?

text.content: Just then, the Tianji Record Fragment suddenly vibrated violently. Chen Ji looked down to see that within the originally blurred patterns, an eye's outline was faintly emerging—the eye was cold, merciless, as if gazing down upon all living beings from the Nine Heavens. Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly turned grave: 'It... has appeared again.'

dialogue.content: (Gripping the fragment tightly) The Heavenly Fate Eye... do you think you can frighten me this way?

text.content: The eye's outline only existed for a moment before dissolving, but Chen Ji knew this was no coincidence. The Heavenly Fate Eye had never manifested its presence so actively before—what did this mean? A warning, or a declaration of war? He took a deep breath and tucked the fragment into his chest. Regardless, the most urgent matter at hand was dealing with the encirclement from the three forces.

He picked up the anonymous letter again, carefully examining the paper's texture, the ink's depth, the brushstrokes' trajectory. The letter appeared ordinary, yet every detail revealed something suspicious. First, the messenger could precisely locate his hiding spot, indicating the sender knew his movements intimately; second, the information in the letter was too precise, not like hearsay but rather firsthand observation.

choice.prompt: The anonymous letter became a crucial clue, and Chen Ji needed to decide his next course of action.

choices.description: Following the messenger's trail might lead to finding the owner of that mysterious 'Qingluan' symbol.
choices.visible_cost: May expose one's whereabouts, drawing attention from other forces.
choices.visible_reward: Might find clues about his sister Chen Nian.
choices.risk_hint: The messenger might be a decoy.

text.content: Chen Ji brought the letter close to his nose and gently sniffed. Intermingled with the ink's fragrance was a faint herbal scent—that was the unique calming incense of Tianqing Sect. His heart stirred; only the Inner Sect of Tianqing Sect could afford such incense. Could this letter have come from someone within the sect itself?

choices.text: Analyze the Situation of All Parties
choices.description: Calmly analyze the relationships between Xuanwu Sect, the Crown Prince's Residence, and the mysterious letter, searching for weaknesses.
choices.visible_reward: Might discover points of conflict among the three forces.
choices.risk_hint: Analysis requires time, the three-day deadline passes in an instant.

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes, arranging all known information in his mind through combinations. What Xuanwu Sect wanted was him as a person, what the Crown Prince's residence wanted was the truth behind the Grand Tutor's death, and that anonymous letter... felt like a third party stirring up trouble in the shadows. The three parties had different objectives and intertwined interests—as long as he could find that delicate balance point...

Sudden hurried footsteps echoed from outside the window, followed by knocking at the door. Chen Ji's body instantly tensed, his right hand already touching the short sword at his waist. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang out: "They're not looking for you, it's the neighbors." Chen Ji relaxed slightly, but didn't let down his guard. He quietly approached the window and peered through the crack—

An middle-aged man in lavish robes was hurrying past, followed by two men in black. The robed man's face flashed in the moonlight, yet Chen Ji recognized him—this was Zhou Jin, a Chief Secretary from the Crown Prince's residence, one of the Crown Prince's most trusted strategists. His personal appearance here meant the Crown Prince's investigation into the Grand Tutor's death had escalated to the highest level.

dialogue.content: (Murmuring to himself) Zhou Jin... it seems the Crown Prince's patience has run out.

text.content: Chen Ji quickly wrote several names in the Tianji Record, then closed the book. Three days, only three days. If he couldn't resolve this crisis before then, his staged death would completely collapse. But what concerned him more was the Qingluan symbol on the letter—that family mark only he and Chen Nian knew. What was going on?

choice.prompt: Time was running out, multiple clues simultaneously pointing toward danger. Chen Ji had to make his final decision.

choices.description: Leave this dangerous imperial capital for a safer place to regroup.
choices.visible_cost: Abandon direct control over the situation
choices.visible_reward: Preserve strength, so he could counterattack morecomposedly later
choices.risk_hint: Once he leaves, he'll lose the chance to interfere with the Crown Prince's investigation

text.content: Chen Ji made his decision. He quickly packed all his belongings, including that crucial anonymous letter. Before leaving, he set a small mechanism in the corner of the ruined temple—if anyone broke in, this device would silently collect a blood sample from the intruder. This was his backup plan.

choices.description: The Qingluan symbol might be the key to finding his sister Chen Nian, worth the risk to investigate.
choices.visible_reward: Might obtain important information about Chen Nian
choices.risk_hint: The investigation might trigger certain people's attention

text.content: Chen Ji's fingers repeatedly stroked the letter paper, the Qingluan's pattern flickering in the candlelight. His sister had been missing for years, yet this letter suddenly appeared... He couldn't let go of any clues related to her. Even if it was a trap, he would step into it himself to take a look.

choices.description: Follow the Qingluan symbol while also setting up a scheme to make the Crown Prince's residence and Xuanwu Sect fight each other. Highest risk, but also greatest reward.
choices.visible_cost: Energy divided, problems could arise on both fronts
choices.visible_reward: If successful, would completely reverse the passive situation
choices.risk_hint: Needs to complete two highly difficult tasks within an extremely short time

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, a flash of determination crossing his eyes. He had never been one to choose—if he decided to do something, he would push it to the extreme. He quickly planned action strategies for both threads in his mind, time was tight, but sufficient. He believed in his own strategy, and believed the Tianji Record would provide him enough foresight.

Just as Chen Ji was preparing to act, the Tianji Record once again grew slightly warm. He frowned and opened the pages, only to see Mo Xiansheng's remnant soul gazing at him, eyes carrying an indecipherable and inexplicable expression.

dialogue.content: (Mo Xiansheng) Lad, I advise you to examine that letter's handwriting carefully. Perhaps, you might remember something... something you thought you had already forgotten.

text.content: Chen Ji unfolded the letter once more. This time, he paid no attention to the content, focusing instead on that unique brushwork. The strokes were fierce in their beginning, gentle in their conclusion, with an almost invisible little hook at the turning point... He had seen this characteristic before, long ago. It was a habit Chen Nian had developed as a child when practicing calligraphy. He had teased her countless times for that peculiar ending stroke.

Chen Ji's hand trembled slightly, an unfamiliar emotion surging within him. If this letter was truly written by his sister, then where was she now? How did she know he was still alive? More importantly—did she have any idea how much danger this letter might bring him? On the Tianji Record Fragment, the outline of the Heavenly Eye manifested once more, as if silently mocking his wavering resolve.

Chen Ji tightly clutched the letter in his hand, his knuckles turning white. After a moment, he released his grip, carefully folding the paper and tucking it into his chest. Whether this was a trap or the truth, he would verify it himself. But for now, he had more pressing matters to attend to—the grave-robbing crisis in three days had to be resolved first.

He lifted his gaze toward the night sky, where the stars had dimmed and dark clouds were slowly pressing in from the distant horizon. A storm was approaching. And he, Chen Ji, stood at the center of this tempest, facing the greatest crisis since faking his death. Yet his gaze was calmer than it had ever been. Scheming the world was precisely his greatest strength—if they wanted to play, he would play along to the very end.

That familiar handwriting flickered faintly in the candlelight, as if coming from a long-forgotten friend... Chen Ji closed his eyes, and his sister Chen Nian's face emerged in the darkness, carrying long-missed warmth, yet also intertwined with countless mysteries. The Heavenly Fate value continued to deplete, the situation kept deteriorating, and he had to find his own way of survival in this approaching storm.
